title: Jewelry Sellers: How to Photograph Rings, Chains, and Diamonds That Actually Sell Online
description: Selling jewelry online is brutal. Here's how to shoot and edit photos that convert—even without a $2,000 macro lens.

blocks.text: Jewelry is the hardest category to photograph. Reflections. Tiny scale. Fuzzy chains. Sparkle that never quite reads on camera. And buyers demand near-forensic detail before spending $200+.
Here's how solo sellers pull it off without a studio.
The Three Killers of Jewelry Photos
1. Bad backgrounds. Any texture, any color cast, any distraction—buyers can't focus on the piece.
2. Fuzzy chain edges. Manual Photoshop selection around a chain? 45 minutes. Poorly done, always.
3. Inconsistent scale. A ring and a pendant filling the same frame confuses buyers about actual size.
Fix these and you A disciplined workflow can make a small catalog more consistent.

The Editing Magic
Here's where most jewelry sellers give up—edges.
The local model attempts to preserve fine edges, but chains, lace, mesh, and reflective details are difficult cases. Inspect the result at high zoom and use manual edge refinement when needed.
Upload your shot, background gone after local model processing, edges intact.
Presenting Sparkle Properly
Diamonds and gems need dark backgrounds sometimes to show fire and brilliance, and white backgrounds other times for marketplace listings.
Solution: Save your product as a transparent PNG once. Drop it onto white for Amazon, black for Etsy hero shots, gradient for social ads. One edit, infinite variations.

Use Rights-Safe Source Images

If a source image contains a watermark, obtain an unwatermarked file from the rights holder or create your own photo. edit-photo does not remove watermarks, and removing ownership marks without permission can create legal and marketplace risks.
The 15-Minute Listing Workflow

items.text: Shoot 5 angles of the piece in your lightbox

blocks.text: Fifteen minutes per listing. Ten listings per week. You're running a professional jewelry operation.
Start Shooting Better Today
